steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 74.32 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk. It is longer than a 72 in stick: splice two, or cut it from a longer log.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the open side on the saw table, with the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 21.1° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the RIGHT. Bevel 11.2° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 2.01 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face, down to 1.80 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Cut 2 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the slanted sawn face on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 45.9° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 35.7° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 8.81 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side, down to 0.50 in along the point. This cut meets its mirror on the centre line.

steps.title: Cut 3 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the open side on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the RIGHT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 0° (blade upright). Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, left of the blade, is only a sliver. This cut meets its mirror on the centre line.

steps.title: Cut 4 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the sawn face that lies on the open side on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 9.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Measure from the first cut and mark: 73.57 in along the point; 61.35 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side; 64.15 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the sawn face that lies on the open side -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 1.84 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side, down to 1.47 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. This cut meets the panel's edge (bevelled to the seam).

steps.title: Cut 5 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the slanted sawn face on the saw table, with the point against the fence, the keeper to the RIGHT of the blade. Mitre 45.9° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 35.7° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Measure from the first cut and mark: 73.57 in along the point; 61.35 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side; 64.15 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the slanted sawn face -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, left of the blade, is only a sliver. This cut meets its mirror on the centre line.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 73.57 in along the point, 64.15 in along the bark corner of the slanted sawn face, 61.35 in along the bark corner of the sawn face that lies on the open side. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as left run 1: flipped over: sawn face against the open side, point back toward the wall.

Saw settings, held as the piece lies in the panel:
22 ends: mitre 30.0°, bevel 9.0° -- the panel's long edge; bevel half the 18.0° seam fold
22 ends: mitre 60.0°, bevel 0.0° -- meets its mirror on the centre line
fitting: Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.
